info.title: WapuPay API
info.description:
WapuPay is a platform that allows users to pay in local currency (ARS) using cryptocurrency (USDT) as the underlying asset.

## Authentication

Two schemes are supported:
- **Bearer JWT** — obtained via `POST /users/login`. Short-lived; refresh with `GET /users/refresh`.
- **API Key** — header `X-API-Key`. Requires `api_enabled = true` on the user account.

> Never send both schemes at once — the server returns `400`.

## How to get an API Key

You can generate the API Key from this same Scalar web UI:
1. Log in with `POST /users/login` using your username and password for the selected environment.
2. Copy the `access_token` returned by login and use it as the Bearer token in the **Authorize** button.
3. Run `POST /users/api-token` authenticated with that Bearer token.
4. That endpoint returns the API token. Use it for server-to-server requests with the `X-API-Key` header.

This works for both **staging** and **production**. The only requirement is to have a user created in the environment you want to use. If you want access to both environments, you must create the account twice: once in staging and once in production.

## Rate Limiting

API Key requests: **60 requests / 60 seconds** (sliding window). Exceeding returns `429`.

## Error Format

All errors return `{ "error": "message" }`.

---

## ARS → Lightning

1. Quote with `GET /transactions/direct-fiat/quote`, `type=crypto_purchase`, `payout_currency=SAT`, `payout_network=LIGHTNING` and exactly one of `amount_ars_cents` or `amount_out`.
2. Create with `POST /transactions/direct-fiat/tentatives` and a Lightning Address in `payout_address` (not BOLT11).
3. Call `POST /transactions/direct-fiat/tentatives/{tentative_id}/funding` and transfer the exact returned amount to the indicated alias/CVU.
4. Poll `GET /transactions/direct-fiat/tentatives/{tentative_id}` while `watch_pending=true`. Only `payout_status=completed` means external delivery.

Purchase amounts use base units: ARS cents, sats and USDT cents. Do not mix them with decimal amounts from crypto → ARS payments. Examples are fictional and are not current quotes.

get.description:
Get a single transaction by UUID or numeric ID. For Lightning deposits with PENDING status, the invoice is checked in real-time and may return COMPLETED.

Use `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` or `X-API-Key: <api_token>`. Do not send both headers in the same request.

Transactions linked to direct-fiat include tentative_id. For a Lightning purchase, the order's executed_transaction_id points to the withdrawal: payment_amount and fee_taken are in sats, while total_amount_taken is in decimal USDT. Do not confuse these display units with the tentative's integer cents. Liquid adds asset_id and, when a txid exists, blockchain_scan_url.

get.description:
Without page or per_page: full legacy transaction list, without swaps, kind or pagination. Send either parameter to get paginated history merging transactions and swaps, newest first; each item has kind=transaction or kind=swap. Defaults: page=1, per_page=7; maximum 50. Deposits linked to historical swaps are excluded in paginated mode to avoid duplicates. Track direct-fiat purchases through /transactions/direct-fiat/tentatives, not as swaps. This list serializes base transactions; tentative_id and Liquid links from the detail endpoint are not added here.

Authenticate with JWT or API Key (never both). Reads only return the effective user's operations. B2B: send `X-Wapu-User-Id` with an owned sub-user UUID.

post.description:
`fiat_transfer` / `fast_fiat_transfer`: fund with crypto to pay ARS (existing contract). `crypto_purchase`: transfer ARS to receive crypto. For Lightning use SAT/LIGHTNING and a Lightning Address. Quote first, then create the tentative, which freezes terms but does not assign a bank account yet. Each POST creates a new tentative; do not replay creation as an idempotent operation. Example amounts and fees are illustrative.

Authenticate with JWT or API Key (never both). Reads only return the effective user's operations. B2B: send `X-Wapu-User-Id` with an owned sub-user UUID.

List all tentatives of the effective user, in every status, newest first and without pagination. Includes crypto → ARS payments and ARS → crypto purchases. Each item includes created_at and public UUIDs of linked transactions. Purchases do not include invoices, credentials or internal receiver IDs.

Return the state of a crypto → ARS payment or ARS → crypto purchase. For purchases, poll while watch_pending is true, even if status is EXPIRED. payout_status=completed confirms delivery; review needs resolution, and settled_to_balance credits the Wapu USDT balance, not Lightning delivery. Alias/CVU disappear when payment is matched, the order is final or an unpaid reservation is released. Linked UUIDs can be fetched with GET /transactions/{id}.

post.description:
Crypto → ARS keeps existing deposit instructions. ARS → Lightning assigns a receiver account and returns alias/CVU and the final amount_ars_cents: transfer exactly that amount, which may differ from the quote by identification cents. It does not return a Lightning invoice. Resets expires_at for the payment window. Repeating this call on an order whose bank instructions were already issued preserves the assignment without duplicating reservations or extending the deadline; alias/CVU only appear while instructions remain valid. On availability/contention 409, retry later; if the fee changed and the error requests a new quote, quote and create again.

Authenticate with JWT or API Key (never both). Reads only return the effective user's operations. B2B: send `X-Wapu-User-Id` with an owned sub-user UUID.

get.summary: Quote a direct-fiat payment or purchase
get.description:
ARS → Lightning: send `type=crypto_purchase&payout_currency=SAT&payout_network=LIGHTNING` and exactly one of `amount_ars_cents` (ARS cents) or `amount_out` (sats). Do not send amount_ars or funding_currency for a purchase. Output example: `?type=crypto_purchase&payout_currency=SAT&payout_network=LIGHTNING&amount_out=10000`. Input example: replace amount_out with `amount_ars_cents=780000` (ARS 7,800). Quotes do not reserve funds or freeze prices: creation freezes terms and /funding assigns the final bank transfer amount. Purchase USDT fields are in cents. For crypto → ARS keep the existing parameters: amount_ars, funding_currency and type=fiat_transfer/fast_fiat_transfer.

Authenticate with JWT or API Key (never both). Reads only return the effective user's operations. B2B: send `X-Wapu-User-Id` with an owned sub-user UUID.

tags.name: Transactions · Direct-Fiat Tentatives
tags.description:
Direct fiat combines a `Deposit` + a `fiat_transfer`/`fast_fiat_transfer` into one orchestrated operation. It lets the client avoid orchestrating the BTC/USDT deposit and the fiat payment separately, and avoids recalculating quotes: the tentative keeps the quote frozen for about 15 minutes.

IDs to follow:
- `tentative_id`: identifies the orchestrating direct-fiat operation and its frozen quote. Follow its status with `GET /transactions/direct-fiat/tentatives/{tentative_id}`.
- `funding_transaction_id`: UUID of the asset deposit transaction generated by `POST /transactions/direct-fiat/tentatives/{tentative_id}/funding` to deposit usually BTC or USDT. Follow its status with `GET /transactions/{id}`.
- `executed_transaction_id`: UUID of the fiat transfer (`fiat_transfer` or `fast_fiat_transfer`) created once the system detects the deposit was completed successfully. Until then, it is `null`. Follow its status with `GET /transactions/{id}`.
- `refund_transaction_id`: UUID of the refund transaction. Follow its status with `GET /transactions/{id}`.
